_comment: Chords Fusion's own 'Change Keyboard Shortcut' prompt refuses to hold, keyed by
the canonical modifier set (fusion.MOD_ORDER order, joined with '+', '' = none).
A value is either a list of bare keys that are reserved with that exact modifier
set, or {'except': [...]} meaning EVERY key is reserved except the ones listed.
Compiled by fusion.py::reserved() against fusion.split()'s canonical form, so a
chord is looked up by its exact modifier set — ctrl+shift (one finger) and
shift+alt (space) are touched only where this table names that exact set.
Source: measured by hand against Fusion's prompt, 2026-09-16. There may be more;
add them here as they turn up.
'surrogate_mods' is the pool a reserved chord is rewritten into when remapd needs
somewhere for Fusion to actually hold it — cmd+alt first, then with one more
modifier at a time, until a slot fusion_set finds free. Never ctrl+shift+cmd or
ctrl+alt+shift+cmd: those are four and five fingers (fusion.FINGER_MODS, 2026-10-16).
'stand_ins' is for a key the prompt will not hold under ANY modifier set — its
hint asks for an alphanumeric key, and Space never lands (2026-09-24). A reserved
chord on one of these keys gets its surrogate on a stand-in letter instead, tried
in order with the same surrogate_mods pool.
'surrogate_avoid' is never a surrogate: chords macOS or Fusion's menu bar answers
before the prompt sees them. The anchor step TYPES the surrogate into Fusion, so
cmd+w's first pick, alt+cmd+w (Close All), closed windows (2026-10-12).
